articles.title: LLM JSON output truncated? A deterministic repair ladder
articles.excerpt: You prompted for JSON. The model returned something that is 95% JSON. json.loads throws. Now what? The two common reactions are both wrong. Reacting with "the API errored" wastes a perfectly good resp…
articles.body: You prompted for JSON. The model returned something that is 95% JSON. json.loads throws. Now what? The two common reactions are both wrong. Reacting with "the API errored" wastes a perfectly good response. Reacting with a pile of regex hacks silently corrupts data — a greedy re.sub that strips a comma inside a string, a naive brace-matcher that trips over a quote in a value. The fix is a repair ladder : a deterministic sequence of progressively more aggressive fixes, stopping at the first that parses, and — this is the part people skip — reporting which rung saved you . What actually breaks LLM JSON Markdown fences: triple-backtick json blocks wrapped around valid JSON. Harmless, constant. Prose around the object: "Sure!

articles.title: Why I Chose a Node.js Queue for 429 Rate-Limit Retry in AI Image Storage
articles.excerpt: An AI image generation job is only half-finished when the bytes exist. In a fintech pipeline, a 429 rate limit or dropped connection can make an upload fail after the image was created, so retry backo…
articles.body: An AI image generation job is only half-finished when the bytes exist. In a fintech pipeline, a 429 rate limit or dropped connection can make an upload fail after the image was created, so retry backoff has to protect the durable hand-off. Short answer: keep generation and object storage upload as separate queue jobs, persist the generated bytes (or a durable temporary reference), and retry the upload with exponential backoff using an object key derived from the job ID. Object storage is the durable sink; the queue owns recovery. Infrai can fit when one REST API and one credential let that queue switch storage vendors without changing its application contract. What does a failed AI image upload actually cost? The expensive term is usually regeneration, not the final PUT.

articles.title: Python Retry with Exponential Backoff and Jitter (stdlib only)
articles.excerpt: Most retry code I see in agent projects looks like this: for i in range(3): try: return call_api() except Exception: time.sleep(2) raise RuntimeError("gave up") It survives a demo. In production it fa…
articles.body: Most retry code I see in agent projects looks like this: for i in range ( 3 ) : try : return call_api ( ) except Exception : time . sleep ( 2 ) raise RuntimeError ( "gave up" ) It survives a demo. In production it fails in four different ways, and each one is its own failure mode. Here's what's wrong and the stdlib-only pattern we ship instead. Problem 1: it retries permanent errors A 401 (bad key) and a 429 (rate-limited) are not the same failure. Retrying a 401 three times burns 6 seconds and a support ticket. Classify first: RETRYABLE_EXCEPTIONS = ( TimeoutError , ConnectionError , OSError ) RETRYABLE_STATUS = { 408 , 409 , 425 , 429 , 500 , 502 , 503 , 504 } Anything outside those lists should fail on the first attempt.

(Image credit: HEO) A commercial satellite has spotted the International Space Station (ISS), giving us a unique view of the orbiting lab from above. What is it? Most of the time, when we see the ISS, it is from down here on Earth or from the viewpoint of the astronauts onboard, peering out the windows at the station's limbs, solar arrays and instruments. But in this snapshot, which was posted on X on Nov. 9 by the Australian company HEO, we can see the station stretched out in all its glory. HEO specializes in using satellites in low Earth orbit to capture images of other spacecraft, though longer-term the company aims to capture observations far out into the solar system.

articles.body: I’ve spent a lot of time with smart telescopes , from relatively inexpensive Seestar models to the original Vaonis Vespera and the Vespera Pro . They all promise essentially the same thing — you put a telescope outside at night, choose something interesting on your smartphone and let the technology take care of the rest. The Vaonis Vespera 3 does that exceptionally well, but after spending several nights with it, I’m convinced it’s designed for a rather different kind of buyer. The telescope’s optical arm folds into its curved body when switched off. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) At $2,490/£2,199, this is hardly an impulse purchase for the beginner who’s curious about astronomy – you could buy several perfectly capable smart telescopes for the same money.

articles.title: Astronomers stunned after James Webb Space Telescope discovers the earliest pair of black hole-powered quasars
articles.excerpt: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have discovered the oldest pair of black hole-powered quasars ever seen. There's just one problem: they shouldn't exist!
articles.body: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have discovered the oldest pair of supermassive black hole-powered quasars ever seen. There's just one problem: they shouldn't exist! The compact quasar pair, spotted with the aid of the Gemini North telescope, has been designated J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, which means "Two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the universe." The compact quasar pair is seen as it was 900 million years after the Big Bang at a time when such supermassive black holes should not have had time to grow to such tremendous masses. Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua isn't just the oldest and most distant quasar pairing ever seen.
